tokyo_hibiya_matsumotoro.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the 1F grill serves curry (European-style roux), omurice, hamburg, fried shrimp, crab cream croquettes and cakes.
tokyo_hibiya_matsumotoro.vegan_detail: Not vegan: omurice, hamburg, seafood, curry.
tokyo_hibiya_matsumotoro.hours_raw: 1F Western grill and garden terrace: daily 11:00–21:00 (L.O. 20:00); closed at New Year (Tabelog). The 3F French restaurant Bois de Boulogne keeps its own hours (listed separately). 1F dinner bookings only; only the terrace open-deck table can be booked by day.
tokyo_hibiya_matsumotoro.notes: [Yōshoku · the restaurant inside Hibiya Park] A long-established Western-food restaurant set in Hibiya Park; this record covers the ground-floor grill and the garden terrace (the third-floor French dining room, Bois de Boulogne, is listed separately). The signature curry is a sweet, fruity, European-style Showa curry. Omurice comes with a choice of sauce and a side such as hamburg, fried shrimp or crab cream croquette. A shrimp and scallop omurice in tomato sauce was ¥1,850; a poulet, cake and coffee set ¥2,800, with seasonal fruit cakes shown at the table. The outdoor terrace is the joy of a fine day (paid special seats exist), and staff seated a party of 12 together. Expect a 30-minute wait at weekends or during park events; only the terrace open-deck table can be booked. Party plans with free-flow are about ¥8,500.

tokyo_sushi_sueyoshi_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Omakase only, so swaps must be arranged with the chef. Nothing is called gluten-free; the course includes soy-sauce-marinated and shrimp-miso-soy-sauce red shrimp, tuna braised in miso, karasumi wrapped in mochi, and on some days soft-roe spring rolls with house XO sauce (2026 reviews).
tokyo_sushi_sueyoshi_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: an omakase of fish and seafood, with clam broth and shrimp miso soup.
tokyo_sushi_sueyoshi_roppongi.hours_raw: Sushi daily 12:00–14:00 (last order 12:30; lunch only with a reservation made by 17:00 the day before) and 17:00–22:00 (last order 20:30) (Tabelog; official site). The official site lists closing days as irregular. From 22:00 to 04:00 the same counter runs as BAR末吉 (Bar Sueyoshi), with 60-minute all-you-can-drink at ¥3,000 (official site). Omakase courses only; seating 90 minutes, all-you-can-drink 60 minutes; arrive on time; seat-only bookings choose a course on arrival (Tabelog). Bookings by phone or online. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 6 counter seats; non-smoking; private hire up to 20. Opened 3 July 2026 (Tabelog).
tokyo_sushi_sueyoshi_roppongi.notes: [Sushi · Roppongi, a six-seat omakase counter steps from the crossing] Opened in July 2026 on the ground floor a few steps from Roppongi Station exit 5: a single hinoki counter for six, omakase only, at a price unusual for Roppongi (¥8,800, or ¥11,000 with an hour of all-you-can-drink sake). The tuna is fresh domestic hon-maguro from まぐろ大善 at Toyosu, a dealer the shop's site says was founded 400 years ago (reviewers link it to Tokugawa Ieyasu), served as rare cuts like neck, cheek and tail; other fish come straight from fishermen around Japan, and you can watch videos of the buying and the tuna cutting as you eat. A course in autumn 2026 ran about 15 to 17 dishes: Nemuro hokke with fresh wasabi, tuna braised in two misos at the counter, karasumi in grilled mochi, smoked mackerel, red shrimp seared with shrimp-miso soy sauce, grilled eel, anago, tamago and brown-sugar ice cream. Diners in 2026 liked the chef's conversation, and one September party got talking with neighbouring guests; one September regular found the second visit less generous (sea urchin had become a ¥1,100 extra). At 22:00 the room turns into BAR末吉 until 4 am. Lunch only with a booking made the day before.

tokyo_tsuyano_koku_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Nothing is called gluten-free. Sushi with red-vinegar rice and many small dishes; the weekday lunch has an udon set and omurice with demi-glace (May 2026); soy sauce and miso are likely throughout.
tokyo_tsuyano_koku_roppongi.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog's listing ticks "vegetarian options" and "particular about vegetables", but no vegan dish is named; the menu is built around fish, sushi and sake snacks, and lunch comes with miso soup.
tokyo_tsuyano_koku_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon–Fri lunch 11:00–14:00 (last order 13:30); every day 17:00–05:00 (food last order 04:00, drinks 04:30) (Tabelog). Lunch had paused and resumed in May 2026 (review). Cover charge ¥1,000 a person; private rooms add a ¥1,000 room fee (¥2,000 in all); karaoke ¥2,000 a person (Tabelog). 50 seats: counter, sofa and box seats, private rooms for 2, 4, 6 or 8; heated-tobacco smoking area (Tabelog; an April 2026 diner notes iQOS is allowed). tokyo_tsuyano_koku_roppongi.notes: [Sake bar · Roppongi, sushi and sake in a basement until 5 am] Down the stairs of a building facing Azabu Police Station, a minute from Roppongi crossing: a back bar lined with sake bottles, a counter, sofas, box seats with what one diner called a nostalgic snack-bar feel, private rooms and karaoke. The draw is the sake list, over 300 labels poured from 90 ml, in tasting flights or all-you-can-drink, served with red-vinegar sushi and small dishes until 5 am. A May 2026 group of three paid about ¥18,000 after a ¥5,000-a-head sake all-you-can-drink of some 30 labels (each guest must order a dish); others come after the last train or simply to stay till the first one. Courses with all-you-can-drink run ¥8,000–¥16,000. On weekdays it serves a cheap lunch: fluffy omurice, an udon set, and a seafood bowl limited to ten. An August 2026 reviewer says it is popular with celebrities and often used by the media for interviews. A ¥1,000 cover applies; English-speaking staff.

tokyo_sushi_hajime_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Nothing is called gluten-free. Nigiri are seasoned at the counter (some pieces marinated or brushed with sauce, e.g. swordfish soaked a day in sake and mirin, October 2026), and the starters include squid shumai with ponzu (2026 reviews).
tokyo_sushi_hajime_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish and seafood counter; the course ends with a crustacean miso soup (October 2026).
tokyo_sushi_hajime_roppongi.hours_raw: Sun–Thu and holidays 18:00–01:00 (last order 00:30); Fri–Sat 18:00–03:00 (last order 02:30) (Tabelog). A 10% late-night charge applies after 22:00 (Tabelog). Bookings online; arrival times in 15-minute steps (July 2026 review). 8 seats at an L-shaped counter (Tabelog; July 2026 review); non-smoking. Cards, IC cards, e-money and QR (PayPay, Alipay and others) (Tabelog). English menu and English-speaking staff (Tabelog). Opened 8 August 2024 (Tabelog).
tokyo_sushi_hajime_roppongi.notes: [Sushi · Roppongi, an 8-seat late-night counter on Imoaraisaka] A minute from Roppongi crossing, on the ground floor facing Imoaraisaka: eight seats at an L-shaped counter, open from 18:00 until 1 am, and 3 am at weekends. The young chef, from Saga and previously at Sushi Ryuta in Roppongi, serves an omakase of ten nigiri with sea urchin, two small dishes and miso soup for ¥7,700, or ¥11,000 with 90 minutes of all-you-can-drink sake and wine. The rice blends rice vinegar and red vinegar, the toppings are cut thick and the rice a little generous, on purpose, the chef told an October 2026 diner, because the course has few pieces. Autumn 2026 courses brought Shiogama hon-maguro, kasugo-dai, three sweet shrimp in one piece, grilled sanma, kinmedai and a purple sea-urchin gunkan; a monthly regular adds the Hajime roll of fatty tuna, salmon roe and eel. There is no kitchen, so starters are simple (July 2026). A September 2026 diner counted about half the guests from overseas; others use it as a second stop. A 10% late-night charge applies after 22:00.

tokyo_sougo_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask, at least two days ahead: the shop asks for allergies and dietary restrictions two days in advance and adjusts dishes (official site). Nothing is called gluten-free, and 2026 courses included fried spring rolls, corn fritters coated in arare, eggplant with somen, sushi in monaka wafers and a kadaif-topped salad; red miso soup and kombu tsukudani come with the rice.
tokyo_sougo_roppongi.vegan_detail: Shojin (Buddhist vegetarian) cooking. The English site says "Shojin vegetarian… (we can also cater to vegan guests)"; the Japanese site says vegan guests can eat with peace of mind. Say you are vegan when booking (two days ahead). Desserts and drinks include a "cream" zenzai and a ginger latte whose milk is not described; one March 2026 diner wrote that the course had fish, which contradicts the shop's own description.
tokyo_sougo_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat lunch 11:30–15:00 (last entry 14:00), dinner 17:30–23:00 (last entry 21:30); closed Sundays and public holidays (official site; Tabelog). 10% service charge on courses, food and drinks (official site). Private room for up to 7, room fee ¥5,000; semi-private room for up to 5, ¥2,000 (official site policy page; Tabelog). Cancellation fees apply (course: 100% same day, 50% the day before). Allergies and dietary needs two days ahead. Bookings via TableCheck, Tabelog or phone. 42 seats: 14 at the counter, tables, box seats, private and semi-private rooms; wheelchair access; designated smoking area; cards, no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Children welcome. Opened 23 February 2015 (Tabelog; the Japanese chef page also says 2015, the English page 2011). A second shop, 淡路宗胡, is at THE PASONA on Awaji Island (official site).
tokyo_sougo_roppongi.notes: [Shojin · Roppongi, modern Buddhist vegetarian kaiseki from a Daigo-family chef] Owner-chef Daisuke Nomura is the eldest son of the family behind 精進料理 醍醐 in Atago, where the chef was third-generation head chef while it held two Michelin stars from 2008 (official site). In 2015 the chef went independent and opened Sougo a minute from Roppongi Station to bring shojin ryori, the vegetarian cooking of Zen temples, to more people: traditional technique with modern touches and a few surprises, in a relaxed room with a counter, tables and private rooms. Dinner is a kaiseki course (¥15,400 or ¥18,700); lunch can be a ¥1,980 tray of seasonal vegetable dishes, rice and red miso soup, a shojin curry, or a lunch kaiseki. The menu changes about every three weeks; 2026 diners remember sushi in crisp monaka wafers, eggplant 'somen' and fried spring rolls, and you may take home the chopsticks and hand towel. The shop caters to vegans and allergies with two days' notice. A 2026 reviewer found the guests mostly from overseas and felt the staff might not understand much Japanese. Closed Sundays and holidays.

roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog: "Owner Chef Daisuke Nomura"; official site)

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the eldest son of the family that runs the shojin restaurant 醍醐 (Daigo) in Atago, Tokyo; built a career as Daigo's third-generation head chef, with two Michelin stars from 2008; went independent in 2015 and opened Shojin 宗胡 (the English page says 2011; Tabelog gives 23 February 2015); teaches and promotes Japanese and shojin cooking in Japan and abroad; named to the Plant Forward Global 50. A second shop, 淡路宗胡, is at THE PASONA, Iwaya, Awaji (official site). A May 2026 diner had heard the restaurant is run by the son of Daigo's owner. Daigo itself is a hidden placeholder in this data (tokyo3_kamiya, name "精進料理 醍醐", address_ja "〒105-0002 東京都港区愛宕2-3-1 201").
chef_bio.philosophy: "I want to cook dishes enjoyable for all guests from every generation, every culture, and every diet… the most memorable dishes are those that give me the opportunity to share moments of gratitude with my guests." (official English chef page).
chef_bio.specialty: Modern shojin kaiseki; sushi in monaka; vegetable sashimi.

tokyo_taisei_yotsuya.notes: [Ramen · Yotsuya, a standing iekei counter at the station] A narrow standing-only counter right by Yotsuya Station's Exit 2, opened at the end of August 2025 as the second shop of Menya Taisei, whose first shop is in Nakano-Sakaue; one diner had eaten here back when the spot was Yokohama Ramen Ryoma. The bowl is iekei: a pork-bone and chicken soy-sauce broth, firm-to-order noodles, nori, spinach and thin chashu, and the house sign promises chicken and soy sauce. October 2026 diners found it refined for the style, strong on soy sauce but easy to finish, and best with a bowl of rice under nori dipped in the broth; the small rice comes with chopped grilled chashu on top. Opinions on the two shops differ: some find Nakano-Sakaue deeper and more chicken-forward, others prefer this one. Buy a ticket (cash only), hand it over, and the bowl comes in minutes; turnover is quick, but there can be a line at lunch and late at night. Hot in summer, cold in winter, and no hooks for coats.

tokyo_oliva_vava_yotsuya.notes: [Italian · Yotsuya, a third-floor hideaway with private rooms] Up steep stairs on the third floor of an old building a minute from Yotsuya Station, a room the shop says was inspired by a cosy restaurant where locals gather in Tuscany's olive groves: a bright counter on one side, tables and a run of private and semi-private rooms for 2 to 24 on the other. At night there are courses and party plans; on one, diners poured from bottles of red and white set by the table (October 2026). Staff ask about dislikes ahead and were flexible for a pregnant guest; one diner waited a while for water before anyone came (October 2026). tokyo_unicoco_yotsuya.notes: [Italian · Yotsuya, a restaurant devoted to sea urchin] "By uni maniacs, for uni maniacs": the owner-chef, a sommelier trained in Italian cooking, travelled Japan tasting sea urchin and opened this shop in 2016 after the summer-only uni festival at the chef's first restaurant, Osteria T, drew fans from around the country. It keeps 15 to 20 kinds of uni at a time, the site says, because the same species tastes different by season and even by beach, and every course turns on a tasting plate of 7, 9 or 12 kinds side by side, then uni pasta, a main and an uni dessert. Diners in 2025–26 compared red, black, bafun, purple and hadate uni, liked the rich ones from Aomori and Hokkaido and the uni from Hagi, and found uni even in the pudding; one parents' birthday got a surprise plate. A blue, sea-themed third-floor room with ocean-like glassware and private rooms. Not every visit landed: a November 2025 pasta lunch disappointed. Reservation only; the à la carte Italian next door, Oliva Vava, is under the same roof.

chef_bio.background: Per the official profile: born in Kagoshima in 1977; came to Tokyo at 26; at 31 enrolled at 辻調理師専門学校 in Abeno, Osaka; after graduating learned cooking and wine at an osteria in Shinjuku and qualified as a sommelier; in June 2012, at 35, opened Osteria T in Yotsuya, whose "夏限定ウニ祭" (summer-only uni festival) drew fans from across Japan; opened unico-co in November 2016 and reopened it after a refit in 2018 to host guests from around the world. The site says the chef tastes sea urchin around the country and joins each region's uni with its local ingredients and the chef's Italian roots. TV: 王様のブランチ (19 October 2019), ぶらり途中下車の旅 (6 February 2021), 全力!脱力タイムズ (9 July 2021), 食彩の王国 (23 July 2022) (official site). The house sake's Yamada Nishiki comes from the Tottori organic grower 杉山信一郎 (official site). The Italian restaurant Oliva Vava (tokyo_oliva_vava_yotsuya) on the same floor takes à la carte orders (official site).
chef_bio.philosophy: "ウニで世界一を目指す" — to be the world's best at sea urchin; keeping 15–20 kinds of a costly, perishable ingredient makes no sense for a restaurant, the site says, but it is worth the risk because guests are moved (official site).

tokyo_seki_tei_ningyocho.notes: [Izakaya · Ningyocho, Aomori seafood and obanzai upstairs by the crossing] A homely second-floor izakaya of 15 seats just off the Ningyocho crossing, built around fish and produce from Hachinohe in Aomori, and run by a chef from Hachinohe (per an April 2026 review). By day it is known for its "service" seafood bowl: about nine kinds of fish and shellfish heaped so high the rice disappears, with head-on red shrimp and baby scallops in the shell, for about ¥1,200, plus a free pot of fish broth to pour over the last of it as chazuke. Arrive before noon; seven people were already in by 11:45 one April 2026 day. At night it is a sake izakaya with daily obanzai, Aomori dishes such as senbei-jiru, Hachinohe mackerel and scallop skewers, and courses from about ¥4,000; a March 2026 diner counted around 100 dishes. Diners praise the value; one in September 2026 found the room worn, with a large TV on. Closed Sundays and holidays.

tokyo_mennosuke_ningyocho.notes: [Ramen · Ningyocho, garlic-salt "Gifu ramen" at a 10-seat counter] A small counter shop a few steps off the main road near Ningyocho station, opened in March 2025, serving what it calls original Gifu ramen. To order (by QR code) the cooks stir-fry pork belly, napa cabbage and cabbage in a pot, add the broth, then the noodles and garlic (October 2026), so the cloudy salt soup tastes of sweet vegetables, pork and a strong hit of garlic, with a ball of red chili paste to stir in at spice level 0 to 5. Diners in 2026 found it lighter than it looks; a Gifu native called it the long-missed taste of home, and an October 2026 diner described it as based on Gifu Tanmen, a local specialty of the Chubu region. Free bean sprouts and pickled mustard greens sit on the counter; most people add the half fried rice set. Expect a short queue at lunch; closed Sundays.

tokyo_a_la_bouteille_yotsuya.notes: [French · Yotsuya, a basement wine bistro under Yoshinoya] Down the stairs below the Yoshinoya on Shinjuku-dōri, a 20-seat bistro opened in 2017 that the shop says is a bistro for a first stop and a wine bar for a second. The cooking is prix-fixe French built on producers the staff have gone to meet: a mosaic terrine of the week's pesticide-free vegetables from Gori-san in Kiyosato, nerve-killed fish from Ishinomaki and Ise-Shima, game bought straight from hunters, and a sea bass in vine leaves and pastry with beurre blanc that has been on the menu since opening. Dinner starts with a black-truffle madeleine; the 5-course menu is ¥6,050, but supplements and a wine pairing can more than double it. About 100 wines, mostly French, and the owner-sommelier's pairings drew praise in 2026, with Greek Robola, a 100-year-old sherry with abalone and non-alcoholic pairings. Diners in 2025–26 call it a hidden spot that feels like a corner of Paris; solo guests eat at the counter, and one June 2026 diner heard that performers from Kioi Hall come here. Lunch only by booking; closed Sundays; ¥550 bread charge.

chef_bio.background: The official site says the shop opened in July 2017 "新宿西口Un Verreを経て" (after Un Verre at Shinjuku west exit), and calls the pâté de campagne refined in the way of "老舗レストラン出身のシェフ" (a chef from a long-established restaurant). The staff visit producers and buy only what they judge good, so they can pass on the producer's character and story; game comes direct from hunters, such as 儀間さん of Ashoro, Hokkaido, who sends only neck-shot deer; vegetables weekly from ゴリーさん in Kiyosato; prosciutto from 尾島博 (Hiroshi Ojima), maker since 1977 (official site; Tabelog menu). A June 2026 diner writes that "the owner kindly explained everything" and an August 2026 diner credits "pairings by the owner-sommelier". The site also sells the chef's French deli dishes online and a French osechi box (2026). No source names the chef or owner.
chef_bio.philosophy: "ワインも食材もこだわり、生産者の想いを伝える店でありながら、どこか気楽に" — particular about wine and ingredients, passing on the producers' feelings, yet somehow relaxed; a place where adults can take their time (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Kiyosato vegetable terrine; sea bass in vine leaves and pastry; game from hunters.

anecdotes.text: "I hear that performers and conductors from Kioi Hall often visit this place. Indeed, there were many signatures on the walls." — June 2026, post-concert gathering.

tokyo_odenya_den_yotsuya.notes: [Oden · Yotsuya, a basement oden counter since 1992] A small basement room on Shinmichi-dōri with one U-shaped counter for 15 around the oden pots, open on weekday evenings since 1992. Beside the classics (daikon, soft-boiled egg, konnyaku, beef tendon) come pieces that go into the pot when ordered and take 10 to 15 minutes: thick beef tongue, house tsukune and ganmodoki, fresh yuba, cherry tomatoes, Camembert, steamed onion, fried mochi, oysters in season, and a fukuro of vegetables and mushrooms. A diner on a fourth visit in December 2025 called it the best of the year and watched two cooks work the left and right pots. Finish with a lemon ramen or dashi chazuke. Calm rather than loud, good alone or with a friend; book or phone ahead. Closed weekends and all of August; smoking is allowed, and the toilet is up on an empty third floor.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner or cooks. chef_bio.specialty: Oden in a gentle dashi; beef tongue and made-to-order pieces.

A February 2026 diner called it the local bistro worth keeping secret and paid about ¥6,000 with two drinks. Cash only; closed Sundays.

tokyo_manyoken_ningyocho.notes: [Ramen · Ningyocho, Hong Kong wonton noodles and dim sum by the station] A Hong Kong noodle and dim sum restaurant half a minute from Ningyocho station, open from 11:00 to 23:00 every day but Tuesday. Tabelog credits the cooking to a dim sum chef trained in Hong Kong with more than 40 years' experience. At lunch it is mostly noodles: plump shrimp wontons, chicken chashu and greens in a soy-sauce or salt soup, often as a set with freshly steamed shumai or har gow (¥1,550 in 2026), or slow-braised beef brisket on noodles or rice. At night the menu turns to dim sum, fried rice, congee and Cantonese dishes, with Shaoxing wine and Chinese teas. The shopfront looks small but the room runs deep, with booths and a counter for solo diners; an April 2026 diner heard Chinese spoken all around and felt abroad, and an October 2026 visitor came after seeing it on TV. No sets on Sundays and holidays; closed Tuesdays.

tokyo_bangkok_peanuts_shokudo_ningyocho.notes: [Thai · Ningyocho, a back-alley Thai canteen open every day] A roomy Thai restaurant at the end of a narrow alley a minute from Ningyocho station, open for lunch and dinner every day of the year but New Year since 2012. The cook, per the shop's own site, is from Uttaradit and learned at Thai street stalls from the age of 15; staff greet you in Thai (October 2026). Lunch is the draw: a mini set of gapao and a curry over rice with a fried egg, salad and coconut tapioca for ¥900, or a green curry for ¥850 with ¥150 add-ons of mini gapao or tom yum noodles. One diner back for an eighth time in October 2026 has worked through Khao Soi, larb gai sets and beef-tendon rice noodles; another came for the khao man gai. At night it serves tom yum goong, grilled pork and chicken, som tam and stir-fries with Thai beers, and courses with all-you-can-drink. Diners find the heat mild and tuned to Japanese tastes; the shop says it will adjust spice and leave out coriander. Everything can be taken away. A September 2026 diner called the prices unbelievably low.

tokyo_kudan_ningyocho.notes: [Shabu-shabu · Ningyocho, a small hot-pot room where everyone picks a broth] An 18-seat shabu-shabu restaurant two minutes from Ningyocho station, where each diner gets a pot and chooses a broth: kombu, Japanese dashi, sukiyaki, medicinal, mala or soy milk, all on the house kombu-and-bonito dashi. The meat is sliced only when you order it (Black Wagyu and Iwate's Iwachu pork are the stars) and vegetables come from a self-serve bar. Dinner is a set with 120 g of meat from about ¥3,600 or an all-you-can-eat course from ¥5,650; diners in 2025–26 praised the marbled beef, with one finding the beef better than the pork. Weekday lunch is a small hot pot with help-yourself salad and rice for about ¥1,000. It fills up early: a February 2026 diner saw the owner or manager working alone and turning the OPEN sign round to keep up. A calm room, popular with groups; closed Mondays.

tokyo_sushi_kaminari_ningyocho.notes: [Sushi · Ningyocho, a young chef's 9-seat omakase counter] A bright nine-seat counter behind a double sliding door in a narrow Ningyocho alley, opened in December 2024 by Daiki Araki (named in a September 2026 review), who trained for ten years at Sushi Saeki and comes from a sushi family, per Tabelog. The chef's home ground is Himeji (official site), and the fish follows: Akashi anago, sea bream and cuttlefish alongside Toyosu catch and tuna from 石司. A course runs to six or seven small dishes, then about ten nigiri on red-and-black-vinegar rice, and ends with a toro-takuan roll and a castella-like tamago (¥27,000; Sunday lunch ¥16,000). Two repeat diners in 2026 note the rice changing and improving, and praise the chef's warmth; one August 2026 diner noted the shop carries the name of the owner's father. There are about 20 sakes, some from Himeji. Book through the shop's site; Sunday is the only lunch.

tokyo_kyushu_satsuki_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Nothing is called gluten-free. The menu leans on fried food (fried oysters, soft-roe tempura, assorted fried plates), gyoza, mentaiko motsunabe and sauce-dressed dishes, and horse sashimi is served with sweet soy sauce.

Online booking; same-day course bookings (June 2026 review); orders by tablet. 100 seats, all in rooms for 2 to over 30 behind roll curtains and shoji (June 2026 review); a smoking area, and 80 smoking seats per Tabelog. Cards, e-money and PayPay. English- and Chinese-speaking staff. Children welcome. Wheelchair accessible. Opened 19 August 2016 (Tabelog). A free whole cake for birthday and wedding after-party bookings (Tabelog remark).
tokyo_kyushu_satsuki_roppongi.notes: [Izakaya · Roppongi, private-room Kyushu izakaya for groups] Four floors above Sushi Sueyoshi, a few steps from Roppongi Station exit 5: a 100-seat izakaya made entirely of private rooms, open noon to midnight every day of the year. The menu is Kyushu comfort food — horse sashimi from Kumamoto, Hakata motsunabe with mentaiko, satsuma-age, charcoal-grilled jidori and yakitori from ¥83 a skewer — with shochu and sake, and most groups book a course with two and a half to three hours of all-you-can-drink for about ¥3,800–¥4,400. Diners in 2025–2026 call it a typical chain-style private-room izakaya: generous, fried-heavy and fine for a party rather than a destination; one in June 2026 found the curtain-and-shoji rooms noisy, another in September 2026 loved the chicken and pork hot pots finished as rice porridge. Tabelog counts 80 smoking seats. Staff speak English and Chinese. Gurunavi lists a second branch, 錦糸町店.

tokyo_wagyu_yakiniku_tanjiro_roppongi.notes: [Yakiniku · Roppongi, all-you-can-eat wagyu by the crossing] On the fourth floor above Wendy's at Roppongi crossing, half a minute from the station: a bright, 60-seat yakiniku house with private rooms, open 11 am to 11:30 pm every day, built around two-hour all-you-can-eat courses of A4-or-better Kyushu black wagyu — 37 items for ¥3,980 Monday to Thursday, 55 for ¥5,980, or 65 with A5 cuts and steak for ¥7,980. tokyo_roppongi_kinme_sushi.notes: [Sushi · Roppongi, omakase with free refills in a basement counter] Down in a basement three minutes from Roppongi Station, eight counter seats and an unusual deal: a course of about 15 dishes, then as many repeats as you like of the nigiri on the blackboard, with all-you-can-drink included in most plans (¥10,000, or ¥15,000 with sake and Yamazaki and Hakushu whisky). A regular writes that the chef earned a Michelin star in Italy and worked in Toronto, and sake lovers in 2026 enjoyed the chef's picks of unusual labels. tokyo_burger_revolution_roppongi.notes: [Burgers · Roppongi, 100% wagyu burgers with halal patties] A small burger and wine bar three minutes down Imoarai-zaka from Roppongi Station, across from Asahi Shrine. Lunch is usually busy, an August 2026 diner says; another came after seeing it on TV. High tables only, so no strollers.

tokyo_oden_to_meshi_hanamido_ueno.notes: [Oden izakaya · Ueno, private rooms a minute from the station] A second-floor izakaya just outside the Asakusa exit side of JR Ueno Station, almost all private rooms, from tables for two up to banquet rooms. Its hook is the starter: for ¥500 you get all the oden you want, simmered in a house blend of dashi made with a long-established dashi wholesaler under a dashi sommelier, from daikon and egg to konnyaku, hanpen, shumai and chikuwa. Diners in 2026 praised the gentle, well-soaked oden (the daikon especially), quick service and a calm room, and ordered grilled mackerel, carpaccio, yakitori, kara-age, fried oysters, agedashi tofu and dashi-maki tamago; several came back many times. Cheap all-you-can-drink coupons and 7-dish courses from ¥4,400 make it a banquet spot. Book online; the phones may be off.

tokyo_halima_kebab_biryani_higashiueno.notes: [Indian/Pakistani · Higashi-Ueno, the biryani house with a lunch line] A long, narrow restaurant with a set-back entrance between Ueno and Inaricho, cooking South Indian and Pakistani food with halal food and no alcohol. The biryani is the draw: basmati rice layered with curry and cooked slowly without stirring, served in huge portions with raita. In October 2026 the chicken biryani set with salad, a tangy red soup and lassi was ¥1,150, and diners queued at lunch; one diner on a fifth visit stops by whenever in Ueno. There are also lamb, mutton, shrimp and vegetable biryani, a Muslim set of half biryani, curry and tandoori, dozens of curries from keema to Goa prawn, and a charcoal tandoor. Staff handled Japanese and English for a 2024 diner; one October 2026 diner found the service curt. On Tabelog's Curry 100 list 2017–2020 and Asian & Ethnic 100 list 2022–2024. Sister shops: Sabera Tikka Biryani, Anas Dosa Biryani, Halal Dosa Biryani.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): ハリマ・ケバブ・ビリヤニ、東上野3-36-7 1F、稲荷町駅から205m、Ueno Mitsui Garden Hotel の近く、毎日11:00〜15:00 (L.O.14:30)・17:00〜22:00 (L.O.21:30)、ランチの予約はコースのみ、50席、禁煙、カード可、子ども可、キッズメニュー、テイクアウト、2014年6月9日オープン、カレー百名店 2017〜2020、アジア・エスニック TOKYO 百名店 2022〜2024、姉妹店は Sabera Tikka Biryani、Anas Dosa Biryani、Halal Dosa Biryani。メニュー (2022年更新): ベジタリアン・ビリヤニ、野菜のカレー、ダールはバター使用。口コミ(2026年10月): チキンビリヤニとラッシーのセット1,150円 (サラダ、スープ、ライタ付き、1,250円という人も)、量が多い、昼は行列、マトンのハーフビリヤニとバターチキンのムスリムセット、3種のカレーとナン、スタッフの態度がよくなかったという声も。2024年5月の口コミ: ハラールの店でお酒はない。

tokyo_coucou_wine_bar_higashiueno.vegan_detail: Ask. Mixed nuts, carrot râpé, lily bulb with silken tofu and fried potatoes are on the menu, but how each is made is not stated; most plates use egg, cheese, ham, liver or meat.
tokyo_coucou_wine_bar_higashiueno.hours_raw: Tue–Fri 15:00–23:00; Sat, Sun and holidays 13:00–22:00; closed Monday and some other days, posted on Instagram and Facebook (Tabelog). tokyo_coucou_wine_bar_higashiueno.notes: [Wine bar · Higashi-Ueno, one owner-sommelier and a cellar] A nine-seat bar on a quiet back street between Ueno and Inaricho, run by one owner who is a sommelier with a long background in French cooking. Some plates are popular dishes carried over from an earlier French restaurant (Tabelog). You can choose a bottle inside the cellar (no prices on the bottles; ask, around ¥10,000 in October 2026) or let the owner pour by the glass to match the food, mostly Burgundy, with natural wines. Diners in 2025–2026 praised the stuffed tomato filled with crab salad, the soufflé omelette over mushrooms, chicken-liver mousse with cocoa, beef cheek braised in red wine and an Earl Grey crème brûlée; in 2026 a seasonal starter of Shine Muscat grapes came first. Open from 15:00 on weekdays and 13:00 at weekends, so good for an afternoon glass. With one person cooking, food takes time. Closed Mondays.

roles: Owner-sommelier, runs the bar alone (Tabelog; reviews)
chef_bio.background: Tabelog's listing (corporate member): an owner-sommelier with long experience in French cuisine, who selects wines from France and around the world, natural wines included, and serves popular dishes carried over from an earlier French restaurant (as the listing puts it, "inherited from the previous French restaurant"). Reviewers in 2025–2026 say the owner runs the place alone. No source names the owner.
chef_bio.specialty: Wine by the glass matched to the food; stuffed tomato; soufflé omelette.

anecdotes.text: "Since the owner runs the place alone, the food takes a bit of time to prepare… they don't serve tea. So, I had a light rosé instead." — December 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): coucou!、東上野3-25-2 鈴木ビル 1F、上野駅・稲荷町駅から徒歩5分、火〜金15:00〜23:00、土日祝13:00〜22:00、月曜と不定休 (Instagram と Facebook で告知)、9席、禁煙、カード・電子マネー・PayPay 可、チャージ500円、2024年1月6日オープン、フレンチの経験が長いオーナーソムリエがフランスを中心に世界のワインを選ぶ (ブルゴーニュ中心、自然派も)、以前のフレンチの店から受け継いだ人気の料理。メニュー (2026年1月): キャロットラペ600円、トマトのファルシ1,050円、百合根と絹豆腐650円、きのこのスフレオムレツ1,200円、牛ほほ肉の赤ワイン煮1,900円、アールグレイのクレームブリュレ800円など。口コミ(2025年12月〜2026年10月): オーナーが一人で営むので料理に時間がかかる、紅茶はない、料理に合わせてワインを提案、お通しにシャインマスカット、蟹のサラダを詰めたトマト、鶏レバーのムース (ココア) 1,050円、グラスワイン1,300円・1,700円、セラーで好きなボトルを選ぶ (約1万円)、白いにんじんを使ったキャロットラペ、鹿肉のバインミー。

tokyo_tonkatsu_gabuu_okachimachi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: every main is a breaded, deep-fried cutlet in fresh breadcrumbs (also menchi katsu and fried shrimp), and each seat must order a set meal.
tokyo_tonkatsu_gabuu_okachimachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a pork-cutlet specialist; every set is pork (menchi katsu and seafood fries too).
tokyo_tonkatsu_gabuu_okachimachi.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–15:00 (food last order 14:00) and 17:30–21:00 (food last order 20:00); closing days irregular, posted on Instagram (Tabelog). Buy tickets at the vending machine from 15 minutes before opening; seated in order of arrival. Reservations through Tabelog only (no phone); dinner is by reservation per an October 2026 review, though a sign welcomes walk-ins. 17 counter seats; each seat orders at least one set meal. Cashless: cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), e-money and QR (PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay, au PAY, Alipay, WeChat Pay); "cash not accepted" (October 2026 review). tokyo_tonkatsu_gabuu_okachimachi.notes: [Tonkatsu · Okachimachi, brand pork at a basement counter] A 17-seat counter around an open kitchen in a basement near Ameyoko, opened in April 2025 by a new company whose head chef trained at Tonkatsu Keita in Nishi-Ogikubo; in about ten months it made Tabelog's Tonkatsu 100 list for 2026, the fastest of that year's new picks. Choose loin or fillet and then the pork: Sanemon, Maru pork, Rokubaku Kurobuta or TOKYO X, from ¥3,278 a set; the cutlets are fried slowly at low temperature in a light coat of fresh breadcrumbs, cut thick and served pink, with a strip of the fat. Rice from a hagama pot, cabbage with a truffle dressing and red miso soup are refilled free. Buy tickets at the machine; it is cashless. In October 2026 diners waited about 30 minutes at Saturday lunch, found premium cuts sold out by evening, and one long-time regular felt the food had slipped since a change of management. Book dinner on Tabelog.

chef_bio.background: Run by 株式会社GAVRIFOOD (Ginza, founded May 2024; representative director 大沼康宏, per a PR Times release of 17 August 2026). This Ueno-Okachimachi shop is the company's first; the second, in Harajuku, opened in 2026 (PR Times). The company's job page says its head chef trained at とんかつけい太, which it ranks fifth nationally in Tabelog's tonkatsu category, and that the company plans 100 shops across five brands in five years. Reviews in May 2025 and October 2026 say the shop is run by a chef from Keita in Nishi-Ogikubo; an October 2026 regular wrote of a change in management. No source gives the chef's name in romaji.
chef_bio.specialty: Brand-pork loin and fillet cutlets; menchi katsu.

anecdotes.text: "A Tonkatsu restaurant run by the chef from Keita in Nishi-Ogikubo. The interior features only a counter… The taste is on par with or even better than Keita." — May 2025.
"On a Saturday just past noon, there were six people ahead of me, and it took about 30 minutes to be seated." — October 2026, Special Premium Loin of Maru pork.
"The change in management has unfortunately led to a decline in attention to detail, flavor, portion sizes… there were more items unavailable than ever before." — October 2026, third visit.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: PR TIMES (2026年8月17日): 株式会社GAVRIFOOD (本社 東京都中央区、代表取締役 大沼康宏、2024年5月設立) が2号店「東京とんかつ がぶう 原宿店」を開業、1号店の上野御徒町店は2025年4月25日の開業から約10か月で「食べログ とんかつ 百名店 2026」に選出、新規選出26店舗の中で最速。求人ページ (herp.careers): 料理長は食べログとんかつ部門全国5位の「とんかつけい太」で腕を磨いた、5年間で5ブランド100店舗の展開を計画。食べログ (店舗会員): 上野4-6-4 OGSⅡ B1F、JR御徒町駅から徒歩2分、毎日11:30〜15:00 (L.O.14:00)・17:30〜21:00 (L.O.20:00)、不定休 (Instagram で告知)、開店15分前から券売機で食券、予約は食べログのみ、カウンター17席、1席1定食以上、禁煙、子ども・ベビーカー可、エレベーターなし、上ロースかつ定食3,278円から (2026年1月のメニュー)、がぶうおまかせ定食6,600円。口コミ(2025年5月〜2026年10月): Nishi-Ogikubo のけい太出身の料理人、低温でじっくり揚げる、ご飯・キャベツ (トリュフのドレッシング)・赤だしはおかわり自由、土曜の昼に30分待ち、夜は売り切れが多い、現金不可、経営が変わって質が落ちたという常連の声も。

tokyo_for_bal_meat_ueno.gf_detail: Ask. The official site says courses can be arranged around allergies ("アレルギーやご予算に応じたコースをご案内いたします"), and grilled steaks, carpaccio and caprese are on the menu, but nothing is described as gluten-free; pasta and pizza are central to the courses.
tokyo_for_bal_meat_ueno.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog's listing ticks "vegetarian options", and the appetizer platter includes ratatouille, herb-marinated olives and house pickles, with a green salad on the menu; everything else is meat, fish or cheese, and no vegan dish is named.
tokyo_for_bal_meat_ueno.hours_raw: Mon–Thu 17:30–22:30; Fri–Sat 17:30–23:30; closed Sundays and holidays, though it may open on a holiday that falls on a Friday or Saturday, and can be hired on Sundays and holidays (Tabelog). The official site (©2021) gives slightly different hours. Reservations taken; changes by the day before, same-day changes are charged. 50 table seats plus a 4-seat counter; private hire up to 80 standing. Non-smoking, with a smoking room inside. Cards, e-money, PayPay and d Barai. Children welcome, with a kids' menu. English menu. Opened 9 February 2017 (Tabelog).
tokyo_for_bal_meat_ueno.notes: [Italian · Ueno, a lively meat bar off the main street] A big, cheerful Italian bar on the ground floor of a sauna-and-capsule hotel two minutes from the Asakusa exit of JR Ueno Station, open since 2017. The house favourite is the appetizer platter, picked from eleven kinds (homemade liver pâté, potato salad with wine-stewed beef, ratatouille, corn terrine and more), then move to grilled meat: black wagyu by the 100 g, an A5 wagyu fillet, lamb, duck confit, or a three-meat platter at ¥2,980. The chef is a certified sommelier (Tabelog), and the official site says the chefs trained in French and Italian cooking; over 50 wines, with glasses from ¥650. Portions are generous (leftovers can be taken home, July 2026), staff are upbeat, and birthday surprises come with music. Friday nights fill with bookings (May 2026), and all-you-can-drink party courses start at ¥6,000. Closed Sundays and holidays.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's listing (corporate member), the chef is a certified sommelier, and the dishes are by chefs with experience in Italian and French cuisine; the official site says the chef trained in French and Italian cooking ("フレンチとイタリアンで修業を重ねたシェフ"). No source names the chef or the operator.
chef_bio.philosophy: "A cheerful hidden Italian restaurant for adults located in the back alleys of Ueno" (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Appetizer platter of up to 11 kinds; grilled black wagyu.

anecdotes.text: "The potato salad appetizer, which includes meat, was exquisite. I often order the assorted platter of three types of meat, as it's reasonably priced." — April 2026, fourth visit.
"It was a Friday night, and the place was almost fully booked with reservation guests. I noticed some walk-in customers had to leave." — May 2026.
"It seems that any leftover food can be taken away… The portion of the steak was quite generous." — July 2026, girls' party plan.

tokyo_shanghai_youshun_menbou_higashiuen.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a noodle house (ramen, dandan noodles, fried noodles, mapo yakisoba) with pan-fried gyoza, kara-age and soy-braised dishes; the fried rice and clay-pot rice are not described.
tokyo_shanghai_youshun_menbou_higashiuen.vegan_detail: Ask. The menu has a clay-pot "temple vegetable" rice, Shanghai New Year shojin dishes, a yuba vegetable roll, wheat gluten with wood-ear mushroom, smacked cucumber and an eight-treasure vegetable stir-fry, but stocks and sauces are not described; most dishes use pork, chicken or seafood.
tokyo_shanghai_youshun_menbou_higashiuen.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–14:30 and 17:00–23:00 (food last order 22:30); Sat 11:30–14:30 and 17:00–22:00 (food last order 21:30); closed Sundays (open to groups of 15 or more by arrangement), Mondays that are holidays, and 31 December–4 January (Tabelog). Cash only (no cards, e-money or QR). A ¥440 charge per table in the evening (お通し代, Tabelog). 30 table seats, semi-private rooms; smoking allowed, but all seats non-smoking at lunch — an October 2026 diner left early because of smoke at night. Menu in Traditional and Simplified Chinese. A June 2026 diner found it open by 11:10.
tokyo_shanghai_youshun_menbou_higashiuen.notes: [Chinese · Higashi-Ueno, Shanghai home cooking and ¥900 lunches] A local Chinese restaurant between Ueno and Inaricho, run with a Chinese chef (July 2026), busy at lunch with office workers and locals. The ¥900 lunch sets bring fried rice or a main dish with a half bowl of shoyu ramen, pickled mustard greens and almond jelly, with cold oolong in patterned teapots on the table. The kitchen's signatures are spare ribs lightly sweetened with rock sugar and mapo tofu (also over fried rice, noodles or crisp yakisoba); there are light dandan noodles, winged pan-fried gyoza, deep-fried yuba rolls and over twenty noodle and rice dishes. At night it's a cheap Chinese izakaya with five Shaoxing wines and ¥280 highballs; smoking is allowed in the evening (an October 2026 diner left early because of it). A June 2026 diner found staff and customers all Chinese. Cash only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: A corporate-member Tabelog listing; a July 2026 review says the food is local Chinese cooking by a Chinese chef. No source names the chef or owner, or gives an opening date.
chef_bio.specialty: Spare ribs with rock sugar; mapo tofu; lunch sets.

anecdotes.text: "With dishes like fried rice, rice bowls, main courses, and noodle dishes, we also got a decent-sized ramen as a side, along with almond tofu—all for just JPY 900." — April 2026, Saturday lunch.
"I was drawn in by the JPY 280 highball. This place features local Chinese cuisine by a Chinese chef." — July 2026.
"The dish featured curly noodles that were crispy on the surface, topped with Mapo tofu… However, the smoke from cigarettes filled the air." — October 2026, after 21:30.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 上海陽春麺坊、東上野3-22-3 津多屋第2ビル 1F、日比谷線上野駅から徒歩3分、稲荷町駅から326m、月〜金11:30〜14:30・17:00〜23:00、土11:30〜14:30・17:00〜22:00、日曜休み (15名以上は相談)、年末年始休み、現金のみ、お通し代440円 (1テーブルにつき)、30席、半個室、喫煙可 (ランチは全席禁煙)、中国語のメニュー、看板は氷砂糖で甘みをつけたスペアリブと麻婆豆腐、紹興酒5種、飲み放題付きコース4,400円・5,500円、上海蟹のコース7,000円。メニュー (2025年10月): ねぎラーメン715円、坦々麺、タンメン880円、鴨の醤油煮込みラーメン1,320円、ふかひれラーメン3,080円、麻婆の料理935〜1,045円、土鍋ご飯1,078円、精進料理、湯葉の野菜巻き、麩ときくらげ。口コミ(2026年2月〜10月): 軽めの坦々麺と半チャーハン、角煮チャーハンと半ラーメン、豚肉ときくらげの卵炒めの定食、ランチセット900円 (チャーハンと半ラーメン、杏仁豆腐)、中華そば850円、羽根つき焼き餃子、湯葉の揚げ巻き、芝麻醤の坦々麺950円、店員も客も中国の人だったという声、ハイボール280円、中国人の料理人、酢豚、麻婆焼きそば、夜はたばこの煙。

tokyo_kaisen_ichiba_happou_ueno.gf_detail: Ask. Tabelog's listing ticks "gluten-free options", and you pick your own ingredients (seafood, meat, vegetables, mushrooms) for a one-person pot, but none of the 13 soups or the sauce bar is described as gluten-free; one soup is sukiyaki-style and noodles, fried bread and dumplings sit on the same counters.
tokyo_kaisen_ichiba_happou_ueno.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog's listing ticks "vegan options", and the soups include a special mushroom soup and a tomato soup with vegetables, tofu and yuba dishes on the counters, but no soup is described as plant-based; several are chicken, beef-bone, pork-bone or clam stocks.
tokyo_kaisen_ichiba_happou_ueno.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–05:00 (last order 04:30), open all year; on the third Wednesday of each month it opens at 18:00 for building maintenance (Tabelog). Reservations for seats taken. Pay per plate: soup ¥500, sauce bar ¥330, plates ¥300–600 (Tabelog menu, prices before tax on some lines); October 2026 diners spent about ¥5,000–8,000 each. 290 seats with private rooms for 4 to 20; non-smoking, smoking area outside. Cards, PayPay, Alipay and WeChat Pay; no e-money. Children welcome, kids' menu. Menus in English, Chinese and Korean, and staff speaking English, Chinese and Korean (Tabelog). Opened 15 June 2026 (Tabelog; Toyo Keizai).
tokyo_kaisen_ichiba_happou_ueno.notes: [Hot pot · Ameyoko, a 290-seat self-serve seafood market open till 5 am] Upstairs in a building in Ameyoko, a vast room laid out like a seafood market: you choose one of 13 soups for your own small pot, then walk the counters and pick plates of live crab, shrimp, abalone, oysters, wagyu, mushrooms, vegetables and Chinese small plates, priced per plate from about ¥300, like conveyor-belt sushi. Crab can be steamed for you and squid and shrimp grilled. The operator, which runs the 銀座八芳 seafood buffet in Ginza, opened it in June 2026 and calls the self-serve shabu-shabu format a first in Japan (Toyo Keizai). Diners in October 2026 enjoyed choosing but warned the plates add up fast (around ¥8,000 each with drinks), praised attentive staff who explain the sauces, and found the room lively and full of Chinese diners even on weekdays. Open 11:00–05:00 every day.

No chef is named.

tokyo_shokudo_bond_higashiueno.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:30–14:30 (last order 14:00) and 17:00–21:00 (last order 20:45); closed Sundays (Tabelog). Reservations taken; lunch is often booked by overseas visitors, so book ahead (September 2026). 14 seats: a 10-seat counter and one table for four. Non-smoking. Cards, e-money and QR (PayPay and others). Children welcome, with a kids' plate; one stroller at a time. English menu and English-speaking staff. Takeout. Opened 1 November 2025 (Tabelog).
tokyo_shokudo_bond_higashiueno.notes: [Sushi · Higashi-Ueno, creative pressed sushi at a small counter] A bright, wood-lined 14-seat sushi bar between Ueno and Inaricho, opened in November 2025, known for torched pressed sushi with unexpected toppings — Fuji salmon with homemade cream cheese and fig, shrimp with tom yum sauce — next to classic Edomae nigiri. The signature Aburi REMIX sets six pressed pieces beside four nigiri (¥4,000); reviewers in 2026 also praised the Toyosu tuna, sashimi and kara-age, while one October 2026 diner found six pieces for nearly ¥2,000 poor value and less traditional than hoped. Lunch adds a ¥1,600 seafood rice bowl with red-vinegar rice and fish soup. The staff speak good English, and many diners are overseas visitors, so lunch is often booked. Families are welcome, with a kids' plate. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.philosophy: "A place where people connect, embodying the spirit of 'Ichigo Ichie'" (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Torched pressed sushi; Aburi REMIX.

tokyo_kakishin_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Nothing is called gluten-free. The signature is fried oysters in a coarse batter, the hot pot is a miso dote-nabe, and oyster rice has come with a shark-fin sauce (2026 reviews). Raw oysters with lemon or ponzu and salt-grilled fish are the plainest dishes; ponzu usually contains soy sauce.
tokyo_kakishin_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: an oyster house; courses add sashimi, Matsusaka beef and chicken.
tokyo_kakishin_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–04:00; closed Sundays and public holidays (Tabelog). Tables and private rooms go first to parties of three or more, and private rooms only to those ordering the omakase course (Tabelog). Busy late in the evening; book early (June 2026 review). 20 seats: counter, tables and private rooms for 2, 4 or 6, including a closed room with a sofa (Tabelog). Non-smoking; a September 2025 diner understood e-cigarettes were allowed only in the private rooms. No cover charge. Cards; no e-money or QR. A free whole cake for birthdays and anniversaries (2026 reviews). Opened 1 June 2016 (Tabelog); ten years old in June 2026.
tokyo_kakishin_roppongi.notes: [Oysters · Roppongi, an oyster specialist open till 4 am] In a basement 30 seconds from Roppongi Station, a 20-seat oyster house that turned ten in June 2026 and stays open until 4 am six nights a week. The shop says its owner comes from a long-established shop in Hiroshima and picks oysters by season and region (Iwate, Ehime, Hokkaido in 2026), along with A5 Matsusaka beef. The famous dish is the "ultimate fried oysters", breaded and fried to order and served with salt and ponzu rather than tartare; a Hiroshima-born diner in July 2026 called them the world's best. Most come for the ¥16,500 omakase — raw, grilled and fried oysters, sashimi, Matsusaka beef, a miso dote-nabe or oyster hot pot and oyster rice — and one diner was told when booking to come hungry. The walls carry celebrity autographs (a TV station is nearby, one diner noted), a regular praises the friendly owner, a June 2026 diner the manager who stayed for a drink, and birthdays get a free whole cake. Closed Sundays and holidays.

tokyo_hyoki_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask when booking. The shop says ingredients can be changed to suit the guest (Tabelog), but nothing is called gluten-free: the shabu-shabu is cooked in a seasoned dashi, the course ends with udon (October 2026), and dishes include grilled mackerel sushi.
tokyo_hyoki_roppongi.vegan_detail: The shop says "Ingredients can be changed to suit the customer. Vegan courses are also available" (Tabelog). Book a vegan course in advance; the standard courses are pork or wagyu shabu-shabu in dashi, with fish dishes.
tokyo_hyoki_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 12:00–15:00 and 18:00–23:00; Sun 12:00–15:00 and 18:00–22:30; last booking 13:30 at lunch and 21:30 at dinner (Tabelog). Cashless only — no cash; cards, IC/e-money and QR (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay and others). 10% service charge at all times. One course per person; some courses need advance booking; a two-hour limit may apply when busy; under-school-age children by arrangement; groups of 20+ sign a confirmation (Tabelog). Cancellation fees apply. 58 seats, all in private rooms, the largest for 28; tatami and sunken seats. Heated tobacco in some rooms, plus a covered outdoor smoking area. Opened 6 May 2016 (Tabelog).
tokyo_hyoki_roppongi.notes: [Shabu-shabu · Roppongi, Kyoto dashi shabu in private rooms] Tucked in a lane off the Roppongi crossing, a 58-seat restaurant made entirely of private rooms that serves Kyoto-style "dashi shabu" as part of a seasonal kaiseki: sweet pork, or wagyu and pork, swished through a light dashi with a heap of green onion, after small seasonal dishes such as mackerel sushi seared at the table and, in autumn, a matsutake dobin-mushi, then udon in the broth and a matcha pudding. Courses start at ¥6,000; the shop offers vegan courses and will change ingredients on request. Diners in 2026 praise the broth and the attentive staff, and it suits business dinners and groups — one company brought overseas visitors in October 2026 — though an August diner found the meat thin and the service green, and one October guest found the cheapest course small. Cashless only, and a 10% service charge applies.

chef_bio.background: Opened 6 May 2016 (Tabelog). The shop says its dashi is inherited from Kyoto (Tabelog). Gurunavi also lists 京都 瓢嘻 京橋店 and 京都 瓢嘻 西麻布店.
chef_bio.philosophy: Kyoto-style shabu-shabu kaiseki in a calm hideaway for adults; ingredients changed to suit each guest (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Dashi shabu with pork and green onion; vegan courses on request.

anecdotes.text: "In a place like this, the quality of the meat is expected, but the broth is truly what makes the difference. And that broth was absolutely delicious." — July 2026.
"During the udon course, I was able to change the flavor with curry powder." — October 2026, farewell party.
"We opted for the most affordable 'Yura Yura' Dashi Shabu course at JPY 6,000, but I felt the portion was a bit small… it seemed the visitors from abroad enjoyed it." — October 2026.

tokyo_amakakeru_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: fish, Hida beef and chicken lead the menu; even the "vegetable" Hong Kong-style yakisoba is seasoned with oyster sauce (December 2025).
tokyo_amakakeru_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 18:00–24:00 (food last order 23:00, drinks 23:30); closed Saturdays, Sundays, holidays and over New Year (Tabelog). Counter charge ¥500 a person, plus 10% service; menu prices include tax. Groups of five or more may be asked to book a course. 10 seats at an L-shaped counter; non-smoking, with a smoking spot at the entrance. Cards; no e-money or QR. Children welcome. Please avoid strong perfume (Tabelog). Opened around August 2024 (an August 2024 diner found it newly opened); a July 2026 diner says it was members-only before opening to the public.
tokyo_amakakeru_roppongi.notes: [Izakaya · Roppongi, a creative Japanese counter for grown-ups] Upstairs in a quiet building a minute from Roppongi Station, a ten-seat L-shaped counter where Chef Sakai (as two July 2026 reviewers name the chef) cooks à la carte Japanese with a few Chinese touches — the shop's line is "more than an izakaya, less than kaiseki". Most dishes are around ¥1,000–2,400, so it works for one plate and a drink or a long dinner. The hits: straw-seared bonito with house onion soy sauce, rare-fried scallops, Hida beef ribeye sukiyaki in a sherry sauce with fluffy egg (order a single slice), wild Gifu ayu in summer, a crisp Kansai-style grilled eel, and Hong Kong-style fried noodles with Sichuan pepper, best mixed with the leftover sukiyaki egg. Sake from small breweries, Japanese wine and craft gin. Weeknights only; a ¥500 counter charge and 10% service apply.

tokyo_hanasato_roppongi.notes: [Teppanyaki · Roppongi, Yonezawa beef and Kyoto cooking with a garden view] Three minutes from Roppongi Station, behind Mikawadai Park and across from the new Azabu Police Station, an 80-seat restaurant laid out like a small museum: a wine cellar at the entrance, a garden view, private rooms, sunken kotatsu rooms and a counter where Yonezawa beef and abalone are grilled on the teppan. Lunch is the easy way in — a Yonezawa beef steak bowl for ¥2,970 with salad, soup and dessert, or set meals to ¥6,050 — while dinner courses run from ¥8,800 to ¥55,000. Diners in 2026 came for birthdays and business meals, praised the private rooms, the strip loin and a gentle beef-tendon soup with Kujo green onion, and one found a fish dish over-sauced and the service uneven. A sister shop is in Gion, Kyoto.

chef_bio.background: Opened 8 March 2012 (Tabelog). The official site lists two shops, 六本木店 and 祇園店. A March 2026 diner notes the chef came out to greet the table.
chef_bio.philosophy: Yonezawa beef teppanyaki and Kyoto kaiseki in a setting that blends a Japanese garden with Western decor (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Yonezawa beef teppanyaki; Kyoto-style courses.

anecdotes.text: "The Yonezawa beef strip loin steak came with unique charcoal salt, wasabi, and ponzu sauce, offering plenty of options to change up the flavors." — June 2026, birthday lunch.

tokyo_amakara_kumakara_ningyocho.notes: [Wild game · Ningyocho, badger, bear and venison from culled animals] A small second- and third-floor dining room at the Ningyocho crossing devoted to Japanese game. The owner, 林育夫, opened in Ningyocho in 1996 and turned to game in the shop's fifteenth year (official site). The meat comes from culled animals: badgers trapped in persimmon, grape and Shine Muscat orchards, whose fat tastes of fruit; moon bears from Akita, Gifu, Nagano and Niigata; Ezo and Yakushima deer; sea lion, kyon and more. Most diners book a course: tataki and heart sashimi to start, Ezo venison off the charcoal, red-wine-braised bear, and badger sukiyaki finished with udon. Bear paw, crow and dolphin tataki are add-ons. First-timers in 2026 were surprised how little gamey taste there was. The badger kakuni became famous through the YouTube videos of Masahiro Higashide, who also held a magazine discussion here (2026 reviews; Tabelog). One June 2026 diner found the service poor. Collect a sticker for each animal you eat. Closed Sundays and holidays.

tokyo_sumibi_yakitori_izawa_ningyocho.notes: [Yakitori · Ningyocho, a calm fifth-floor charcoal-grill counter by the station] A new (September 2025) yakitori restaurant on the fifth floor of a building beside Ningyocho station exit A3, with a nine-seat counter in front of the charcoal grill and tables by the windows. Staff ask how you like the chicken cooked, and diners praise the timing and explanations; one lunch diner in October 2026 found the upselling pushy. The owner is a certified sake sommelier. Opened 15 August 2024 (Tabelog).
tokyo_sanseira_chongqing_hotpot_ueno.notes: [Hot pot · Ueno, Chongqing mala on the third floor of UENO3153] A large, bright hot-pot restaurant right in front of Ueno Station's Shinobazu exit, opened in August 2024, with partitioned tables, a few private rooms and window seats over the station area. Choose your broths (fiery Chongqing mala, tonkotsu, tomato or mushroom), then load the pot with lamb, beef, pork, vegetables, mushrooms and shrimp balls, and mix your own dipping sauce at the sauce bar, where sweets and snacks are free. Diners in 2026 found the mala truly numbing and spicy (even the mildest level), the ingredients fresh, and the room busy with Chinese families and office workers; several wished for instructions on how to order and eat. Book on weekends. No cards — PayPay, Alipay or WeChat Pay.

"It's a wonderful place where dogs are allowed inside!… It would be great if there were instructions on how to eat everything, as there weren't any provided." — September 2026.
"I visited on a Friday night. It seemed fully booked, so I recommend making a reservation… I was glad that the desserts were all-you-can-eat!" — October 2026.

tokyo_sakana_utage_ueno.notes: [Izakaya · Ueno, private rooms a minute from the station] A fourth-floor izakaya by JR Ueno Station where every seat is in a private room with a door, open from 11:00 to midnight, so popular for daytime drinking, office parties and groups. The food is standard izakaya fare — sashimi, a three-meat platter, a light 'Taiwanese' motsunabe, yakitori, seared mackerel — and reviewers in 2025–2026 rate it as good value rather than gourmet, with fast drink service from a call button; one called it a chain-style place, another found the finishing dishes of a course weak. All-you-can-drink comes as courses or à la carte (a ¥500 table charge and two dishes each). Smoking reports differ: ask.

tokyo_tori_no_ichi_ueno.notes: [Yakitori · Ueno, brand chicken from a former French chef] A large, modern chicken restaurant a block from Ameyoko, opened in November 2023, where a former French chef cooks regional brand chickens and jidori: charcoal-grilled skewers, chicken sashimi (three cuts, limited servings), yukhoe, thigh tataki with hyuganatsu ponzu, a shaliapin chicken steak and a creamy jidori oyakodon or zosui to finish. Dinner starts with a chawanmushi; courses run from mizutaki to a ¥10,000 premium menu. Weekday lunch is a ¥1,000 yakitori bowl with soup, tofu and a drink, grilled to order. Private rooms and sunken seating for 2 to over 30 make it a party venue; diners in 2026 praised friendly, quick staff. A Shinjuku West Exit shop was due in 2025 (a September 2026 review).

tokyo_nobuchan_ueno.notes: [Yakitori · Ueno, cheap skewers and stew until 4 or 5 am] A long, casual izakaya on Nakamachi Street, a street of bars and clubs (and touts), open from late afternoon until 04:00 most nights and 05:00 at weekends. Prices are low (stew ¥600, small plates ¥350–500, a ¥500 table charge in April 2026), regulars keep bottles here, and you order by phone app. In April 2026 the staff were from elsewhere in Asia, with varying Japanese. Smoking is allowed. Tabelog announces a second shop in Otsuka.

tokyo_kitashinchi_yakiniku_satsuma_roppo.hours_raw: Evenings 18:00 until 08:00 the next morning (last order 07:30) (Tabelog; the shop text says "Open until 8 AM" and "Open on Sundays and holidays!", and it opens over New Year). Tabelog's day-by-day table lists these hours only for days around holidays and marks every weekday closed, which contradicts the shop's own text and 2026 reviews of early-morning visits; check before going. A 10% late-night charge applies after 22:00. Booking online is easy, even same day (May 2026 review). 15 seats: 10 at the counter, tables for up to 7. E-cigarettes only. Cards, IC/e-money and QR (PayPay, au PAY, Alipay, WeChat Pay). English menu and English-speaking staff; Tabelog ticks halal options. Opened 23 February 2023 (Tabelog).
tokyo_kitashinchi_yakiniku_satsuma_roppo.notes: [Yakiniku · Roppongi, Osaka yakiniku until 8 am] The Roppongi branch of さつま, a yakiniku shop the Tabelog text says has been loved in Osaka's Kitashinchi for over 40 years, with a Ginza branch too. Fifteen seats, mostly a counter, and the hours are the point: it runs from 6 pm to 8 am, so it fills up after the bars close — a seven-time regular finds it busier in the early morning than in the evening, and an October 2026 diner came at 5:30 am and ordered the outside skirt five times. Regulars swear by the salt tongue, outside skirt, liver and yukhoe, with mountain-jellyfish kimchi on the side; the Roppongi shop also has Kuroge wagyu tongue and cheek you won't find at the other branches. Courses from ¥7,000 suit first-timers. A 10% late-night charge applies after 10 pm; e-cigarettes are allowed. A May 2026 diner reckoned about 70% of the customers were international visitors; English menu and English-speaking staff.

chef_bio.background: Opened 23 February 2023 (Tabelog). The official site for 北新地焼肉さつま 銀座店 describes the Ginza shop as the Kitashinchi shop's first Tokyo branch ("大阪北新地より創業40年"). A November 2025 reviewer writes that the shop "is run by the same owner as Shiraiishi Ramen"; no other source read confirms it.

Reopened in June 2026 as TORIBAKA PREMIUM (Tabelog shop text; a July 2026 diner calls it revamped from the earlier Toribaka); the listing's opening date is 17 August 2023. 16 seats: 8 at the counter and two tables of 4. tokyo_toribaka_premium_roppongi.notes: [Oden · Roppongi, chicken-broth oden in a basement] Down the stairs of the building that houses Kitashinchi Yakiniku Satsuma, on Imoarai-zaka three minutes from the station: a 16-seat oden bar that reopened in June 2026 as TORIBAKA PREMIUM. Each piece of oden comes in your choice of two broths, a rich chicken paitan or a light dashi with a house usukuchi soy sauce, and the chicken dishes — toriten, grilled liver, wings — use young Miyazaki chicken. Reviewers in 2026 found it good value for Roppongi, with a cosy counter and kind touches (staff re-cut the daikon into four when two more friends arrived); two say it is run by the beauty company Esthe Pro Labo, which supervises its additive-free drinks, and one July visitor was entertained by a manager who had been a magician for 20 years. A February 2026 diner, before the reopening, found the broth too salty and the staff indifferent. Heated tobacco only; ¥300 cover.

tokyo_tsukiyo_ni_kome_no_meshi_takei.notes: [Japanese · Roppongi, seasonal courses and donabe rice behind an unsigned door] Down the stairs of an old building in a lane off Roppongi-dori, through a door with no sign, an 18-seat Japanese restaurant with a counter and private rooms whose courses build up to rice cooked in a clay pot. You pick from several regional rices — four varieties on one April 2026 night — and whatever you can't finish goes home as onigiri. The ¥13,200 course changes monthly: clam chawanmushi, a seasonal hassun, sashimi, fish such as kinki or sawara, buri shabu in winter, ayu confit in summer, and homey touches like dashimaki tamago and soy-milk pudding. A regular on a 28th visit in October 2026 calls it the place for Japanese food in Roppongi, and a birthday booking was met with oysters and caviar. Allow time to find it: two diners went into the building next door first.

tokyo_izakadokoro_tamura_roppongi.notes: [Izakaya · Roppongi, a Showa-era counter for skewers and oden till dawn] On a back street off Enma-zaka, a small L-shaped counter with a nostalgic Showa feel that staff told one diner has been going for about 30 years. Chicken skewers are grilled over charcoal in front of you — the liver, hearts and big, juicy sasami come a little rare because the chicken is fresh — alongside oden, a chicken soup limited to three a day, and crisp cabbage with sweet meat miso. Drinks are cheap and generous: an October 2026 visitor had all-you-can-drink with potato salad, oden, dashimaki and five skewers for ¥3,000, and groups can hire the whole counter with no time limit. Open late most nights (Tabelog says to 5 am Wednesday to Saturday; the shop's own site says to 8 am). Smoking is allowed. The sign is easy to miss, and Google Maps may lead you round the back.
